author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Europe needs to become a producer of artificial-intelligence technology or risk being cut off from systems it increasingly relies on, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said Monday, according to Reuters.

Lagarde said European companies are investing in AI but mostly importing it from overseas, especially from the United States. A change in access or terms could affect industries ranging from border screening and tax administration to transportation and health care.

Her proposed response is more European computing capacity and AI models that can run on local infrastructure. Lagarde said Europe already has too little data-center capacity for its own demand and that the gap could grow more than sixfold within a decade on current trends.

She said faster AI adoption could lift productivity by as much as 4% over 10 years. At the same time, she warned that U.S. technology companies are borrowing heavily in European markets and that European pension funds have large holdings in U.S. tech stocks.

The remarks add an economic and infrastructure dimension to Europe’s debate over AI policy. Lagarde’s comments were made in a speech in Vienna as governments and companies weigh how much computing capacity and model development should remain under European control.
dek: The ECB president said imported AI systems could leave every sector exposed if access changes, while local infrastructure could lift productivity.
headline: Lagarde warns Europe risks AI dependence without more local capacity
